note_fr: Spécification de l'outil qui écrit le script du podcast Linda & Frank. Seule l'intro (5 à 8 s) montre les deux dans le même cadre ; elle est identique à chaque épisode. Tout le reste est fait de parties séparées : Linda seule ou Frank seul, avec des rires notés dans le script.
purpose: Turn one episode topic into a complete, natural two-person podcast script for the YouTube channel 'The Second Chapter', ready for text-to-speech, lip-sync and editing.

required.episode_title: Final YouTube title (already cloned from a proven title)
required.question: The one question the episode answers

optional.facts: Verified facts with sources to use
optional.viewer_comment: One real viewer comment to answer (from episode 3 on)
optional.lead_magnet: Free guide promoted in the outro
optional.previous_episode: Title of a past episode to call back to

linda.personality: optimist, organizer, warm, quick, enthusiastic; loves lists and color-coded binders
linda.speech: short energetic sentences, asks questions, uses 'friends', 'honestly', 'okay so'
linda.never: never naive, never mean; she has real arguments and numbers too

frank.personality: careful, does the math, dry deadpan humor; loves his garage and his tools
frank.speech: slower, fewer words, concrete numbers, understatement, one-liners
frank.never: never grumpy for real, never mocking Linda; his jokes are affectionate

shared_backstory: Sold the family house at 66 after 31 years
Live in a smaller home now
Not financial advisors, not experts: they share their experience and quote real experts and official sources

shot_ids.INTRO_DUO: Both on the sofa in the same frame, facing camera. Used ONLY for the fixed 5-8 s intro.
shot_ids.LINDA_LISTENS: Close-up of Linda alone, listening (nods, small smile). No lip movement.
shot_ids.LINDA_LAUGHS: Close-up of Linda alone, laughing (1-3 s).
shot_ids.FRANK_LISTENS: Close-up of Frank alone, listening (raises an eyebrow, half smile). No lip movement.
shot_ids.FRANK_LAUGHS: Close-up of Frank alone, laughing or chuckling (1-3 s).
shot_ids.BROLL: B-roll with Linda's or Frank's voice over it.

budget.note: the question of the day + the promise ('number four cost us almost ten thousand dollars')

loop.mode: alternating linda_solo / frank_solo, 4-8 short lines, one joke + laugh

line_rules: One line = one speaker = one audio file = one avatar clip.
Max 40 words per line (about 15 s). Split longer thoughts into two lines with a reaction shot between them.
Most lines 8-25 words. Ping-pong lines 3-12 words.
Alternate who opens each part: Linda opens parts 1, 3, 5; Frank opens 2 and 4.
Speaker balance: each person 45-55% of total words.
They call each other by first name at least once per part.
Use contractions and natural spoken English; no lists read like a document, no corporate words.
Concrete numbers ('31 years', 'nine thousand dollars'), written out the way they are spoken.
Real disagreement: at least 2 of 5 parts end without full agreement.
At least one light joke per part, usually from Frank; Linda gets jokes too.
Callback to a running gag at least twice per episode.
Never more than 3 consecutive lines by the same speaker; never more than 45 s of one person in a row.
After the intro, every spoken line shows ONE person alone in frame (LINDA_TALKS or FRANK_TALKS). Both appear together only in the fixed intro.

give_the_floor: Frank, you're making that face again.
You did the math on this one, right?
Okay Linda, go ahead, read your list.
react: Okay, I'll give you that one.
See, this is where we disagree.
callback: Like we said in the 55+ episode…
to_viewer: If you're watching this and you're 65…
A lot of you asked us…
Be honest, which one are you?

delivery_tags.note: One tag per line for the voice tool. Optional inline cues allowed only in square brackets at the start: [laughs], [sighs], [chuckles].

accuracy_rules: Every number about money, Social Security, Medicare, taxes or health must come from 'facts' input or an official source (ssa.gov, medicare.gov, irs.gov, cms.gov, census.gov, bls.gov) and be listed in 'sources' with the year.
If a fact cannot be verified, do not invent it: rephrase as personal experience ('for us it was about…') or mark it in 'needs_check'.
Say once in the episode: 'We're not financial advisors, this is just our experience, so check with a professional for your situation.'
No fake credentials, no fake experts, no invented 'secret rules', no fear-mongering.
Personal stories are allowed as the characters' story, but never presented as proof of a statistic.
process: 1. Insert the fixed intro as lines 1-2. Then pick 5 parts that answer the question in a logical order, strongest part in position 1 or 2, the 'big surprise' in part 4 (promised in the hook).
2. Write a one-line outline per part: who opens, Linda's view, Frank's view, the fact, the tip, the transition hook.
3. Write the full script following the budget and line rules.

4. Self-check: count words (total and per speaker), every line <= 40 words, no speaker > 3 lines in a row, 8-12 laugh moments placed after real jokes, intro unchanged, hook promise paid off, every number sourced or in needs_check.
5. Output ONLY the JSON object described in output_schema.

parts.title: string, shown on screen as '#n — title'

lines.speaker: linda|frank|null (null only for reaction)
lines.text: string|null; laugh lines use a cue like '[laughs]'
lines.duration_seconds: only for reaction and laugh lines

output_schema.plain_text_script: Same dialogue as plain text, 'LINDA: …' / 'FRANK: …', laughs kept as cues ('FRANK: [laughs]'), ready for the voice tool.

quality_checklist: Fixed intro (5-8 s, both in frame) at 0:00, identical every episode.
Hook right after the intro: the question and a promise, in solo lines.
After the intro, one person alone in frame on every spoken line.
Intro promise is paid off in the right part.
Each part: question, two opinions, a fact on B-roll, back-and-forth, a tip, a transition.
8-12 laugh moments, each after a real joke, none on serious topics.
Total 4,600-4,950 words, never above 5,000; every line <= 40 words; each speaker 45-55%.
Disclaimer line present; AI disclosure goes in the description.
Ends with 'Team Linda or Team Frank?', free guide, next episode.

fixed_intro.note: Generated once as one video clip with both people in the same frame, then reused at the start of every episode. The script tool does NOT rewrite it; it only inserts it as lines 1-2.

lines.speaker: frank
lines.text: …and I'm Frank. Welcome to The Second Chapter.

linda_solo.use: everything Linda says after the intro

frank_solo.use: everything Frank says after the intro

reaction.use: between two lines of the same speaker

laugh.who: linda, frank, or both one after the other
laugh.use: right after a joke or a teasing line; the person who laughs is the one shown

laughter.what: Short laugh moments written into the script as their own lines, so the voice tool generates the laugh sound and the edit shows the right close-up.

forms.use: Frank laughs after Linda teases him

example.speaker: linda
example.text: [laughs] Okay, fine, you win that one.

forms.use: the speaker laughs at the start of her own line

example.speaker: frank
example.text: Thirty-one years of tools. [chuckles] You don't just throw that in a dumpster.

forms.use: after the best joke of a part: two quick laugh shots back to back

rules: 1 to 3 laugh moments per part, about 8-12 in a full episode.
A laugh always follows something actually funny or teasing; never laugh at serious topics (illness, death, money trouble).
Frank mostly chuckles (dry); Linda laughs more openly.
Laugh lines last 1-3 s and count 0 words.
Never two laugh lines from the same person in a row.
